title: Replace the dual write with an outbox

task.text: `OrderService` saves the order, then publishes; if publishing fails, the event is lost.

Write the message into the **outbox** in the same transaction as the order, and let a **relay** publish it later. `Shop.place` and `Shop.deliver` must keep working for callers. `Db`, `Message` and `Broker` are given.

items: `OrderService(Db db)`: `place(id)` saves the order and calls `tx.enqueue("OrderPlaced", id)` in one `inTransaction`. It must not know the broker.

`Relay(Db db, Broker broker)`: `int pump()` publishes `db.pending()` oldest first and calls `markPublished(id)` only after the broker accepted it. Stop at the first `IOException`; return the number sent.

checks.title: A placed order is saved and announced
OrderService no longer talks to the broker
Order and outbox row share one transaction
The relay keeps rows until acknowledged
The relay preserves order across failures

hints.text: Two systems cannot commit together, but one database can. What if the "message to send" becomes a row written in the same transaction as the order? Who then sends it?

`OrderService` calls `tx.saveOrder` and `tx.enqueue` inside one `inTransaction`. A new `Relay` reads `db.pending()`, publishes each row, and only afterwards calls `db.markPublished`. `Shop` connects them.
